title: Persistent intrusive tinnitus with normal audiometric thresholds

patient.chiefConcern: Persistent bilateral high-pitched tinnitus despite normal conventional thresholds

stages.title: 1. Extract the clinical story

options.text: Tinnitus characteristics, impact, noise history, otologic symptoms and relevant hearing concerns
Assume normal thresholds mean no further history is needed
Ask only whether the patient wants amplification

stages.feedback: A normal conventional audiogram does not replace a complete tinnitus history.

stages.title: 2. Interpret the findings
stages.prompt: The case has normal thresholds from 0–8 kHz with a high-frequency dip beyond the conventional range. What is the appropriate reasoning?

options.text: Recognize tinnitus can occur despite normal conventional thresholds and avoid inferring a hearing-aid indication from tinnitus alone
Normal thresholds prove tinnitus is not real
The high-frequency dip automatically requires hearing-aid fitting

stages.feedback: The case is intended to demonstrate tinnitus with clinically normal conventional thresholds and to avoid inappropriate amplification.

stages.title: 3. Check for red flags
stages.prompt: What should screening do in this case?

options.text: Screen for relevant otologic/neurologic red flags while recognizing that the supplied presentation is bilateral and non-pulsatile
Skip screening because the audiogram is normal
Label the case as an emergency solely because tinnitus is persistent

stages.feedback: The standardized workflow retains red-flag screening without automatically converting persistent tinnitus into an emergency.

stages.title: 4. Select management
stages.prompt: Which management direction is most consistent with the case objective?

options.text: Education and individualized tinnitus management/support based on impact, without automatically fitting hearing aids
Fit hearing aids solely to suppress tinnitus

stages.feedback: The protocol specifically highlights navigating tinnitus with a normal audiogram and avoiding inappropriate hearing-aid fitting.

stages.title: 5. Justify the decision
stages.prompt: Which explanation best supports the plan?

options.text: Tinnitus management is guided by the patient's tinnitus impact and needs; normal conventional thresholds do not by themselves justify amplification
A normal audiogram means no intervention can be offered

stages.feedback: The clinical reasoning task is to separate tinnitus management from an automatic hearing-aid indication.

stages.title: 6. Plan follow-up

options.text: Tinnitus impact, patient coping, hearing/otologic changes and response to the selected management approach
Only whether thresholds remain exactly normal
No follow-up because the audiogram is normal

stages.feedback: Outcome monitoring remains appropriate even when conventional hearing thresholds are normal.
